references.text: The preceding account of the healing of the officer's servant in Capernaum, which occurs just before Jesus' journey to Nain and provides context for his travels through the towns of Galilee.

Here too it is described that Jesus went from town to town and village to village preaching, accompanied by the twelve and many others – a similar pattern where Jesus travels with his disciples and large crowds.
The crowds followed Jesus, just as they did on the way to Nain. The pattern of large crowds following Jesus repeats throughout the Gospel of Luke.
Large crowds followed Jesus from Galilee and other regions, corresponding to the description in Luke 7:11 where a great crowd accompanied him to Nain.
A large crowd followed Jesus, a recurring motif in the Gospels that also characterizes Luke 7:11.

Elijah went to Zarephath and raised a widow's son from the dead – an event Jesus himself refers to (Luke 4:25-26), which forms the background for the similar raising of the widow's son in Nain that follows in Luke 7:12-17.

Elisha raised the Shunammite's son from the dead. This Old Testament parallel to the upcoming resurrection in Nain is important, since Nain lies near Shunem, and the crowd in Luke 7:16 compares Jesus with the ancient prophets.
Jesus himself refers to Elijah being sent to the widow of Zarephath, establishing a typological connection between Elijah and Jesus – a connection fulfilled when Jesus raises the widow's son in Nain.
